source.author: Al Brooks
source.chapter_title: Need Two Reasons to Take a Trade

conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode

candidates.name: TwoReasonsRequiredToEnter
candidates.quote: you need two reasons to take a trade, and any two reasons are good enough.
candidates.description: A meta-gate on every entry: require at least reasonCount (2) independently-true qualifying conditions from an enumerable list of 'reasons' (signal-bar quality, MA pullback, breakout pullback, always-in pullback, support/resistance test, counting setup, weak opposite signal bar, failure-of-something) to be true on the signal bar before allowing the entry, unless one of the single-reason exceptions (R26-04, R26-05, R26-07) applies.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (gates whether any other entry signal may be taken)

complexity.reason: the market of 'reasons' Brooks lists mixes filters, patterns, and exits from many other chapters; a design decision is needed to pick and wire the concrete sibling conditions this counts before it can be coded

notes: This is the chapter's central, most distinctive idea.

Brooks's bulleted list of 'possible reasons' (good signal bar, MA pullback, breakout pullback, always-in pullback, S/R test, dueling lines, high 2/low 2, double top/bottom, final flag reversal, high 3/low 3 wedge flag, high 4/low 4 flag, weak opposite signal bar, failure of anything) is almost entirely references to primitives already mined in the trends and ranges chapters (reversal bar, two-bar reversal, ii, wedge, double top/bottom, breakout pullback, always-in); none of those list items are re-mined here as new candidates.

candidates.name: NoCountertrendInSteepTrendUnlessPriorBreakOrOvershoot
candidates.quote: if there is a steep trend, never trade countertrend, even if there is a high or low 2 or 4, unless there was first a prior significant trend line break or trend channel overshoot and reversal.
candidates.description: Block any countertrend entry (including counting setups like high2/high4) while the trend is steep, unless a significant trend-line break or a trend-channel overshoot-and-reversal has already occurred first.
candidates.pseudocode:
// research/hard: 'steep trend' and 'significant trend line break' need a trend-line/channel-line projection and a slope threshold
allowCountertrendEntry = !isSteepTrend[0] || priorSignificantTrendLineBreak[0] || priorTrendChannelOvershootReversal[0];

complexity.reason: needs a trend-steepness measure plus trend-line/channel-line break and overshoot detection from pivots

notes: Also notes it is 'far better' if the trend line break had strong momentum rather than a sideways drift; recorded as a strengthening condition, not split into its own candidate.

candidates.name: BarCountingSetupDirectionMustMatchTrend
candidates.quote: a high 2 is an entry in a bull trend or at the bottom of a trading range and not in a bear trend, so if there is a steep bear trend, you should not be looking for high 2, high 3, or high 4 buy setups.
candidates.description: H1/H2/H3/H4 buy-counting setups are only valid in a bull trend or at the bottom of a trading range, never in a bear trend; L1/L2/L3/L4 sell-counting setups are only valid in a bear trend or at the top of a trading range, never in a bull trend. This gates the counting-setup primitives defined elsewhere, it does not itself detect a reversal.
candidates.pseudocode:
allowHighNBuySetup = isBullTrend[0] || isAtBottomOfTradingRange[0];
// mirrored: allowLowNSellSetup = isBearTrend[0] || isAtTopOfTradingRange[0];
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (gates the H1-H4/L1-L4 counting-setup entries defined elsewhere)

complexity.reason: 'bull trend' / 'bear trend' / 'bottom or top of a trading range' are the always-in / trading-range research concepts flagged throughout the corpus

notes: Bar counting setups are explicitly NOT trend reversal patterns per this passage; recorded as a direction-match filter only.

candidates.name: StrongTrendSingleReasonPullbackEntry
candidates.quote: anytime there is a strong trend, you must enter on every pullback that does not follow a climax or final flag reversal, even if the pullback is just a high 1 in a strong bull spike or a low 1 in a strong bear spike.
candidates.description: Exception to R26-01: in a strong trend, a single reason (any pullback, even a bare high1/low1) is sufficient to enter, as long as the pullback does not follow a climax or a final-flag reversal.
candidates.pseudocode:
// research: 'strong trend', 'climax', and 'final flag reversal' are research-grade concepts defined/assumed elsewhere
singleReasonExceptionApplies = isStrongTrend[0] && isPullbackInTrend[0] && !followsClimax[0] && !followsFinalFlagReversal[0];

complexity.reason: depends on the undefined-in-this-chapter concepts of strong trend, climax, and final-flag reversal

candidates.name: TrendLineOvershootReversalBarSingleReasonEntry
candidates.quote: Also, if there was a trend line overshoot and a good reversal bar, you can fade the move and expect the trend to resume. The only other time that only one reason is needed to enter a trade... is when there is a second entry.
candidates.description: Exception to R26-01: a trend-line (or trend-channel-line) overshoot followed by a good reversal bar is, by itself, a sufficient single reason to fade the overshoot and expect the trend to resume.

complexity.reason: needs trend-line/channel-line projection from pivots plus a reversal-bar-quality test

candidates.name: SecondEntrySetupPrimitive
candidates.quote: By definition there was a first entry, so the second entry is the second reason.
candidates.description: Shared primitive for this chapter: a 'second entry' is a same-direction setup that forms within a few bars after an earlier same-direction setup either failed to trigger or triggered and quickly reversed. Defined here so R26-07 can reference it.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (pattern classification used as a signal precondition)

complexity.reason: needs to track a recent failed/reversed same-direction setup across a bar window, not just the current bar

notes: Likely duplicates a second-entry primitive already mined in the trends book's chapter 10 (second_entries.json); the dedup pass should merge them.
Defined locally here since chapter 10 was not part of this mining pass.

candidates.name: SecondEntrySingleReasonSufficient
candidates.quote: The only other time that only one reason is needed to enter a trade, whether in a trading range or in a trend, is when there is a second entry.
candidates.description: Exception to R26-01: whenever the current setup is a second entry (R26-06), that alone is sufficient reason to take it, in either a trend or a trading range.

candidates.name: DuelingLinesConvergence
candidates.description: Shared primitive: two independently-drawn lines (e.g., a trend line and a trend channel line, or lines from two different swings) project to approximately the same price near the current bar, each independently suggesting support/resistance there; their convergence reinforces a reversal or test signal at that level.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (pattern classification used as a signal precondition)

complexity.reason: needs two independent trend-line/channel-line projections from pivots and a proximity test between them

notes: Listed only as one bullet item here ('Dueling lines.') but used substantively as a named setup in chapter 28's worked examples; defined here since this is the first chapter of this mining batch to name it.

candidates.name: WeakSignalBarAtRangeExtremeReversalReason
candidates.quote: Weak high 1 or high 2 signal bar at the top of a trading range when you are looking for a short. Weak low 1 or low 2 signal bar at the bottom of a trading range when you are looking to buy.
candidates.description: A high1/high2 short signal bar that is weak (small body, poor close position) forming at the top of a trading range is itself a countertrend (long) reason, since the failed continuation attempt suggests the range top will hold; mirrored for a weak low1/low2 signal bar at the bottom.
candidates.pseudocode:
isWeakSignalBar = (close[0] - low[0]) / (high[0] - low[0] + epsilon) < weakCloseThreshold; // for a bear (short) signal bar, weak = closes in the lower part of its range
reasonPresent = isAtTopOfTradingRange[0] && (isHigh1SetupSignalBar[0] || isHigh2SetupSignalBar[0]) && isWeakSignalBar;
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (counted as one of the 'reasons' in R26-01)

complexity.reason: combines an existing trading-range-extreme context test with a signal-bar-weakness ratio and the H1/H2 counting-setup primitives

candidates.name: FailedProfitTargetReversalSignal
candidates.quote: A failure to reach a profit target, like the market reversing at five or nine ticks in an Emini scalp.
candidates.description: Price approaches within a small, fixed number of ticks of a plausible profit-target extension beyond a recent extreme (e.g., a signal bar) but reverses just short of or just beyond it; record this near-miss/failed-extension as a countertrend reversal reason.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (counted as one of the 'reasons' in R26-01)

complexity.reason: 'expected profit target' is not defined generically in this chapter; a design decision is needed to pick a concrete reference extension before this can be coded

candidates.name: FirstMovingAverageGapPullbackEntry
candidates.quote: If there is a strong trend, be ready for... the first moving average gap pullback.
candidates.description: In a strong trend, the first pullback that leaves a gap between price and the moving average (i.e., the pullback does not touch the average) is itself a qualifying reason.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (counted as one of the 'reasons' in R26-01)

complexity.reason: needs an EMA distance test and a persistent since-trend-start counter of qualifying pullbacks

notes: Likely duplicates the moving-average gap-bar primitives from ranges chapter 13 (13_twenty_gap_bars.json); recorded here since this chapter names it as a distinct 'reason'.

candidates.name: FirstMovingAveragePullbackEntry
candidates.quote: if there is a strong trend, be ready for the first moving average pullback, for any two-legged pullbacks to the moving average
candidates.description: In a strong trend, the first pullback that actually touches the moving average (the first MA touch of the trend, or the first in more than N bars) is itself a qualifying reason.
candidates.pseudocode:
touchesMovingAverage = low[0] <= movingAverage[0] && high[0] >= movingAverage[0]; // long-side touch test
reasonPresent = touchesMovingAverage && barsSinceLastMovingAverageTouch >= minGapBars;
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (counted as one of the 'reasons' in R26-01)

complexity.reason: needs an EMA touch test and a persistent bars-since-last-touch counter

notes: The 'first in more than 20 bars' detail comes from the chapter's worked example (bar 2, Figure 26.1), used here as the default minGapBars.

candidates.name: TightTradingRangeEntryGate
candidates.quote: In a tight trading range like this, you should never enter in either direction until after either one of the following events: a large trend bar breaks out of the pattern by at least three ticks and you have waited for that bar to fail, or there is a small bar that you can fade near the top or bottom of the trading range.
candidates.description: In a tight trading range, block all entries until either (a) a large trend bar breaks out of the range by at least breakoutTicks and then fails (closes back inside), or (b) a small bar forms near the range's extreme that can be faded.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (gates whether any other entry candidate may be taken)

complexity.reason: 'tight trading range' is a design-decision concept (bar overlap / range-tightness measure) not defined in this chapter

candidates.name: ScaleInLimitEntryAtPriorSwingLow
candidates.quote: One countertrend approach is to buy a half-size position on a limit order placed at the level of the prior swing low, and a second limit order to add on two points lower.
candidates.description: First leg of a countertrend scale-in in a bear trend: place a half-size buy-limit order at the price of the most recent swing low, expecting a bounce off the level of the prior low.
candidates.book_order_type: buy limit order at the level of the prior swing low

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection to locate the prior swing low

notes: Part of the chapter's 'buying new lows in a bear trend' scale-in method (R26-14/15/16/17 together).

candidates.name: ScaleInAddOnLimitEntry
candidates.quote: and a second limit order to add on two points lower (you are trying to scale into your long position).
candidates.description: Second leg of the scale-in: while the first (half-size) entry from R26-14 is open and unfilled on its own target, place a second buy-limit order addOnDistance below the first entry's fill price to complete the full position.
candidates.book_order_type: buy limit order addOnDistance below the first entry

complexity.reason: needs the first scaled-in entry's fill price as a reference, on top of R26-14's swing-pivot dependency

candidates.name: ScaleInProfitTargetExit
candidates.quote: If your one-point profit target is filled before the second buy order gets filled, you take your profit, cancel that other buy order, and look to buy a new swing low.
candidates.description: If only the first (half-size) scale-in entry is filled and price reaches a fixed profit target before the add-on order fills, exit the first entry there (and, by implication, cancel the pending add-on order).
candidates.book_order_type: limit order to take profit on the first (half-size) entry only

complexity.reason: needs to distinguish whether the add-on order has filled yet, i.e. track partial position size, not just MarketPosition

candidates.name: ScaleInExitAtOriginalEntryPriceAfterSecondFill
candidates.quote: Once the market rallied up to your original entry, you could have exited your entire position, having made a two-point profit on your lower entry and having been breakeven on your first buy.
candidates.description: Once both scale-in entries (R26-14, R26-15) are filled, exit the entire combined position once price returns to the first (original, higher) entry's fill price -- breakeven on the first entry and a profit on the lower add-on.
candidates.book_order_type: limit order to exit the whole position at the original (first) entry price

complexity.reason: needs to remember the first scale-in leg's individual fill price separately from the position's blended average entry

rejected.quote: Many of these one-tick false breakouts like those at bars 2 and 3 occur in the first minute or two of a countertrend 5 minute entry bar. Breakouts that occur in the final minute of the bar tend to be more reliable...
rejected.reason: needs intrabar/tick-level timing data (where within the bar the breakout occurred), which is below the resolution of a completed OHLCV bar

rejected.quote: the price action entry off the 5 minute chart (insert) had about a 45 cent risk... or use the traditional 5 minute price action entry (on a stop below the bar that tests the exponential moving average)
rejected.reason: compares an entry signal computed on a second, finer bar series (the 1 minute chart) against the 5 minute strategy's own bars; the engine trades one bar series at a time

chapter_summary: The chapter's core idea is a meta-gate on every entry (R26-01: need at least two independent 'reasons', with three named single-reason exceptions for a strong-trend pullback, a trend-line-overshoot reversal bar, and a second entry), plus a same-direction filter tying counting setups to trend direction and a ban on countertrend entries in a steep trend without a prior trend-line break. Most of Brooks's bulleted list of 'possible reasons' just names primitives already mined elsewhere (reversal bar, ii, two-bar reversal, wedge, double top/bottom, breakout pullback) and is not re-mined here. The chapter also contributes a weak-signal-bar-at-range-extreme reason, a failed-profit-target reversal reason, first-MA-touch/first-MA-gap pullback reasons, a tight-trading-range entry gate, and a distinct 'buying new lows in a bear trend' half-size scale-in method with its own limit-entry, add-on, and two exit candidates (R26-14..17). The dedup pass should note that R26-06 (second entry) and R26-11 (MA gap pullback) are likely near-duplicates of primitives in the trends book's chapter 10 and this book's chapter 13, respectively, which were not part of this mining batch.
